before: boolean stores true or false. && requires both sides to be true; || needs at least one true side; ! reverses a Boolean result.
&& skips its right side when its left side is false. || skips its right side when its left side is true. This is short-circuit evaluation.
denominator != 0 checks that the divisor is nonzero before 10 / denominator is evaluated. Reversing the order would lose that protection.
System.out.println prints a Boolean as true or false. It does not turn a skipped operation into a successful one.
Expected output or behavior: true. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Predict both the final Boolean and whether division executes for inputs 0, 2, and 20. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A boolean is true or false. && means both checks must be true. || means at least one must be true. `!` reverses true and false.
Java reads && and || from left to right. With &&, a false left side skips the right side. With ||, a true left side skips the right side. This skipping is called short-circuiting.
A divisor is the number you divide by. denominator != 0 checks that it is not zero. Putting this check before && keeps the later integer division from using zero.
Printing a boolean shows true or false. A skipped check does not run; Java already has enough information to decide the combined answer.
The program prints true. The divisor is not zero, and ten divided by two is greater than one.
The quiz changes only the divisor to zero. Start again at the left check and decide whether Java reaches the division.

choices: It prints false and skips the division.
It divides by zero and throws an error.
It prints true because the division was skipped.
after.explanation: The left side is false. With &&, that makes the whole condition false, so Java skips the division.
